principles: Smallest shippable slice that produces the paper C2 data proof
Reuse existing sign/verify/digest primitives, don't reimplement
Honest labeling: local-key single-host ≠ Authority strong proof
Soundness via an adversarial contract test, not an A/B rate
drivers: DONE stories only have LOCAL evidence today
C2 must be adversarially demonstrated, not just described

options.name: Build a NEW bundle from LOCAL evidence + local-key signature + offline re-verify
pros: Ships without the Authority server (Tier-C unblocked separately)
Hermetic, demoable now; contract test = paper C2 proof
cons: Local-key signature is weaker than a server-verified receipt — must be labeled honestly

options.name: Require an Authority-server SIGNED gate-decision proof
cons: That signing path does NOT exist yet — it is the Tier-C blocker; would make slice 1 unshippable

options.name: Static source-only check (grep the evidence files)
cons: Not a real verifier; proves nothing about forgery/freshness; not paper-grade

chosen: Build a NEW bundle from LOCAL evidence + local-key signature + offline re-verify
rationale: Only this option ships now (the server path is the Tier-C blocker), reuses the existing primitives, and yields the adversarial contract-test table that doubles as the paper's C2 data proof. The local-key/single-host scope is labeled honestly; Authority cross-host signing is the explicit follow-up.

preMortem.scenario: The local-key signature is read as the Authority strong proof / overclaim
preMortem.trigger: Bundle/verifier output omits the single-host caveat
preMortem.mitigation: Verifier output + bundle field explicitly mark 'local-key, single-host; Authority cross-host signing is Tier-C, deferred'

preMortem.scenario: The contract test passes vacuously (verifier returns reject for everything, or the authentic case never tested)
preMortem.trigger: Missing the authentic-ACCEPT control or not asserting each tamper flips the verdict
preMortem.mitigation: Include an authentic bundle that MUST be ACCEPTED + assert each tamper class moves ACCEPT→REJECT with the correct reason code; assert 0 false-accept AND 0 false-reject

preMortem.scenario: Recomputing materialHash from a real git tree is infeasible in a hermetic smoke
preMortem.trigger: Smoke would need a git fixture
preMortem.consequence: Can't test the freshness conjunct hermetically
preMortem.mitigation: Offline verifier takes currentMaterialHash as an input (the caller computes it from the tree, as the gate already does); the contract test feeds a mismatched currentMaterialHash → must REJECT (stale)
